chunks: I read a reply from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) to a man from his companions. After this [having praised God]:

I hereby advise you to fear God; for God has taken the responsibility for whoever is pious toward Him to turn them from what He abhors toward what He loves, and to provide for them from where they do not expect.

So beware of being among those who fear for [other] servants [of God] because of their sins while feeling themselves safe from punishment for their own sins. For God, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be deceived concerning His Paradise, nor can what is with Him be attained except by obedience to Him, God willing.

key_terms.أَمَّا بَعْدُ: amma ba'd — the classical formulaic transition phrase used in letters and sermons after praising God
key_terms.بِطَاعَتِهِ: by obedience to Him — the sole means of attaining divine nearness and Paradise
key_terms.تَقْوَى اللَّهِ: taqwa of God — God-consciousness and piety; the state of mindful devotion and avoidance of what displeases God
key_terms.ضَمِنَ: guaranteed/took responsibility — used to express that God Himself has taken on the obligation to fulfil a promise for the pious
key_terms.لَا يُخْدَعُ عَنْ جَنَّتِهِ: cannot be deceived concerning His Paradise — meaning no outward show of religiosity or self-delusion fools God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about taqwa and God's guarantee for the pious?
ai.summary: In this letter attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the Imam advises an unnamed companion to embrace taqwa (God-consciousness/piety) as the foundation of spiritual life. The letter highlights a critical moral contradiction: those who are quick to judge others for their sins while remaining blind to their own — a form of self-deception incompatible with genuine faith. The Imam emphasizes that God's Paradise is not attained through wishful thinking but solely through sincere obedience. The passage reflects the genre of epistolary counseling prominent in early Shia tradition, where Imams communicated ethical guidance in writing to distant followers.
word_analysis: I advise you / I enjoin upon you
